data.description:
## Context / Problem

`docs/user-guide.md:423-440` and `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md:57-67` advertise `module_size_trend` and `cap_change_events`, but `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:248-275` no longer exposes those IDs. Janitor is now a concrete consumer, changing the prior no-consumer decision that removed placeholders.

## Approach

Implement both metrics from Git history in the existing metrics subsystem. Preserve the structured `unavailable` contract when history, Git, or required analyzer data is absent; never fabricate zero or placeholder values. Register, document, and test the metrics through the existing CLI/registry paths.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py`
- metric registry/schema/CLI composition
- user guide and maintenance runbook
- focused Git-history fixture tests

## Testing

Use temporary Git histories for growth and cap-change cases, plus shallow/no-Git/unavailable controls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `module_size_trend` reports Git-derived module-size history with source and confidence metadata.
- [ ] `cap_change_events` reports Git-derived module-cap changes with source and confidence metadata.
- [ ] Missing history, unavailable Git, and insufficient evidence produce the existing structured `unavailable` result rather than a zero/placeholder.
- [ ] Registry, CLI, schema, user guide, and runbook expose the implemented metrics consistently.
- [ ] Focused Git-history and unavailable-path tests pass.
data.title: Implement Git-backed module-size trend and cap-change metrics
